The history of the twentieth century revolved to a large 
extent around the (a) reduction of inequality between 
classes, races, and genders. Though the world of the year 
2000 still had its share of hierarchies, it was nevertheless 
a far more equal place than the world of 1900. So people 
expected that the egalitarian process would continue and 
even accelerate. In particular, they hoped that globalization 
would (b) spread economic prosperity throughout the 
world, and that as a result people in India and Egypt 
would come to enjoy the same opportunities and privileges 
as people in Finland and Canada. An entire generation 
grew up on this promise.
Now it seems that this promise might not be fulfilled. 
Globalization has certainly benefited large segments of 
humanity, but there are signs of growing inequality both 
between and within societies. Some groups increasingly 
(c) monopolize the fruits of globalization, while billions are 
left behind. Today, the richest 1 percent own half the 
world’s wealth. This situation could get far worse. The 
rise of AI might eliminate the economic value and political 
power of most humans. At the same time, improvements 
in biotechnology might make it (d) impossible to translate 
economic inequality into biological inequality. The superrich 
will finally have something really worthwhile to do with 
their enormous wealth. While up until now they have only 
been able to buy little more than status symbols, soon 
they might be able to buy life itself. If new treatments 
for extending life and upgrading physical and cognitive 
abilities prove to be (e) expensive, humankind might split 
into biological castes.

44. 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
45. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: Billy는 겨울의 대부분 동안 아팠다.
선생님은 엄마에게 Grace의 학업에 관해 말했다.
엄마는 Grace가 Billy를 기쁘게 했다고 말했다.
Grace는 책을 모두 읽을 수 있다고 엄마에게 말했다.

Grace는 다시 수업 시간에 소리 내어 책을 읽었다.
* 확인 사항
◦답안지의 해당란에 필요한 내용을 정확히 기입
(표기)했는지 확인하시오.
One day while Grace was in reading class, the teacher 
called on Billy to read a sentence from the board. He 
had been sick most of the winter and had missed a lot 
of school. Billy stood to read the sentence, but he didn’t 
know all the words. Since (a) she had been listening to 
the class, Grace read it for him. Billy sat down, 
redfaced and unhappy.
